Maxwell's Demon

An apparatus for the trapping of single atoms, after J. C. Maxwell (1867)

Chambers in microgravity (orbital laboratory)

The atom isn't a billiard ball. It sticks to whatever it strikes for a random time, then leaves at a random angle (Knudsen's cosine law) a little hotter than before. Its temperature is its speed, and its speed is your score.

A Gillund Labs game · gillundlabs.com

Select mode

Guard the open side of a three-walled vacuum chamber with one paddle: drag anywhere on the screen, or use W/S, ↑/↓ or the mouse. An atom that slips past you is lost. Your score is the hottest temperature you reach.

A closed box, two chambers, one trapdoor, and a hot gas and a cold gas mixed together. Hold anywhere (or Enter) to open the door. Separate them, hot atoms on one side and cold on the other, before collisions blend them, or crowd atoms onto one side. Your score is the entropy you remove from the gas, minus k_B ln 2 for every door opening your memory has to record.

Each player drags on their own half of the screen (or uses W/S for the left paddle and ↑/↓ for the right). The walls are top and bottom. When an atom escapes past a player, the opponent scores a point.

Element shop

Elements unlock in order from light to heavy. Buy element Z for Z coins (you earn 1 coin per paddle hit, plus 1 coin per whole µK of your best temperature when a game ends), or win it for free by reaching its threshold temperature while playing element Z−1, or by ending a Sorting game that includes element Z−1 with a net entropy reduction of at least 2 + ⌈Z/3⌉ k_B. Sorting pays 1 coin per k_B of net entropy removed. Coins and unlocks are shared by all modes. Every element starts at the same on-screen speed, so heavier atoms start (and score) hotter.

Settings

Optional. Hold a bank card or ID card (ISO/IEC 7810 ID-1, 85.60 mm wide) against the screen and drag the slider until the outline is exactly as wide as the card.

85.60 mm

The check samples 200,000 exit angles and fits them to cos θ and cos² θ.

Paused

Tap Resume, or press Space, P or Esc
